title: Computer Architecture
body:
[[Motorola 68000]] 

The design of a machine as a programmer sees it: what registers exist, what
[[Instructions]] there are, how big a word is, how memory is addressed. This is the
**instruction set architecture**, the contract between hardware and software, and it is what
this course teaches on the 68000.

Distinguish it from **organisation** or microarchitecture: how that contract is actually
implemented in [[Digital Logic]]. Two chips can share an architecture (same instructions,
same registers, same binaries run) while being organised completely differently inside, one
with a [[Cache]] and a pipeline and one without. Architecture is what you program against;
organisation is what [[COMPUTING MACHINERY 2]] opens up.

The 68000's architecture in one paragraph: a [[VonNeumann]] machine, 16-bit data bus and
24-bit [[Bus|address bus]] giving 16MB of address space, eight general data registers
`d0`–`d7` and eight address registers `a0`–`a7`, operations in three sizes (`.b`, `.w`,
`.l`), a [[Status Register]] carrying the [[Status Bits]], and two privilege levels (user
and [[Supervisor State|supervisor]]).
